seo_title: About ElectraSim — Free Browser-Based Circuit Simulator
seo_description: Learn about ElectraSim — who built it, why it exists, and what makes it different. A free, browser-based electrical circuit simulator for students, teachers, and electricians.
hero_heading: Built for Everyone Who Touches a Wire
hero_sub: ElectraSim started from a simple question: why is there no free, modern, browser-based tool for learning and simulating household electrical circuits?
mission_body:
ElectraSim exists to make electrical circuit education **free, accessible, and interactive**. Whether you're a student studying for an exam, a teacher preparing a classroom demo, an electrician planning a wiring layout, or simply a curious person who wants to understand why flipping a switch turns on a light — ElectraSim is built for you.

We believe the best way to learn electricity is to **see it in action**. That's why every component in ElectraSim behaves exactly as it would in the real world: switches break circuits, MCBs trip on overload, bulbs glow when current flows, and faults light up in red so you can diagnose them immediately.

values.title: Always Free
values.body: No paywalls, no premium tiers, no ads. ElectraSim is and will remain 100% free for everyone.

values.title: Privacy First
values.body: Your circuits stay in your browser unless you explicitly export or share one. Share-link fragments are not sent to our servers. No account required, no tracking cookies.

values.title: Performance
values.body: 60fps simulation on any modern device. Offline-capable PWA. Instant load. No installation ever.

values.title: Education First
values.body: Every feature is designed to teach, not just simulate. Real fault detection, real component behaviour.

tech_body:
ElectraSim is a fully **client-side web application**. Your browser performs the simulation and stores circuits locally; only an export or share action you initiate transfers circuit data. Share links keep their payload after the URL's `#` fragment, which is not sent to our servers. The circuit simulation engine is written in TypeScript and runs in a dedicated Web Worker so circuit solving stays outside the main interaction path.

The production editor uses an accessible SVG renderer with automatic dense-circuit detail and animation limits. A **PixiJS WebGL prototype** remains development-only until it reaches editing, accessibility, and export parity. The site and blog are built with **Astro** for maximum SEO and performance, with content managed through **Sveltia CMS**.
